en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated it to us: Abdullah ibn al-Harith informed us, from Ibn Jurayj: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir narrating from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "If there were to be ill omen in anything, it would be in the dwelling, the servant, and the horse."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If it exists, then it is in the woman, the horse, and the dwelling"—meaning ill omen.

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us: Utbah ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Hamzah ibn Abdillah ibn Umar, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If ill omen were in anything, it would be in the horse, the dwelling, and the woman."
Harun ibn Abdillah narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he did not say "a reality."

Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hakam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, that he heard his father narrating from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "If there were to be anything real in ill omen, it would be in the horse, the woman, and the house."

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim and Hamzah, the two sons of Abdullah, from their father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (Second chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya, Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (Third chain) and Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim and Hamzah, the two sons of Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (Fourth chain) and Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me; (Fifth chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq; (Sixth chain) and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us; all of them from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), regarding ill omen, the like of the hadith of Malik. None of them mentioned contagion or bad omens in the hadith of Ibn Umar except Yunus ibn Yazid.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to us—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah and Salim, the two sons of Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission and no bad omen, and ill omen is only in three things: the woman, the horse, and the house."

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas narrated to us; (Second chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah and Salim, the two sons of Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Ill omen is in the house, the woman, and the horse."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "There is no contagious transmission and no bad omen, and I like good omens." He said: It was asked: "And what is a good omen?" He said: "A good word."

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas: that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission and no bad omen, and I like good omens: a pleasing word, a good word."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no evil omen in the night-bird, and no bad omen, and I love a good omen."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to me: Abd al-Aziz ibn Mukhtar narrated to us: Yahya ibn Atiq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission and no bad omen, and I love a good omen."

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me; (Second chain) and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated it to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us; both from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, the like of it. And in the hadith of Uqayl: "from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)" and he did not say "I heard." And in the hadith of Shu'ayb he said: "I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)," as Ma'mar said.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah: that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "There is no bad omen, and the best of it is the good omen." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what is the good omen?" He said: "A good word that one of you hears."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "There is no contagious transmission, no Safar, and no ghoul." And I heard Abu al-Zubayr mentioning that Jabir explained to them his saying: "and no Safar." Abu al-Zubayr said: Safar pertains to the belly. So it was said to Jabir: "How?" He said: "It used to be said: worms of the belly." He said: "And he did not explain the ghoul." Abu al-Zubayr said: "This is the ghoul that transforms or leads astray."

Abdullah ibn Hashim ibn Hayyan narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Yazid—and he is al-Tustari—narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no ghoul, and no Safar."

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir; (Second chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no bad omen, and no ghoul."
Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated it to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Hatim, Hasan al-Hulwani, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Abd said: narrated to me, and the other two said: narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah narrating that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission," and he would also narrate along with that: "The owner of sick cattle should not bring them to the owner of healthy cattle," the like of the hadith of Yunus.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—and they were close in wording—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission," and he also narrated that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The owner of sick camels should not bring them upon the owner of healthy ones." Abu Salamah said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate both of them from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then Abu Hurayrah later remained silent regarding his saying: "There is no contagious transmission," and stood firm on: "that the owner of sick camels should not bring them upon healthy ones." He said: So al-Harith ibn Abi Dhubab—and he was a cousin of Abu Hurayrah—said: "I used to hear you, O Abu Hurayrah, narrate to us along with this hadith another hadith which you have remained silent about; you used to say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is no contagious transmission.'" But Abu Hurayrah refused to acknowledge that and said: "The owner of sick camels should not bring them upon healthy ones." Al-Harith kept disputing with him regarding that until Abu Hurayrah became angry and spoke in the Ethiopian language. He then said to al-Harith: "Do you know what I said?" He said: "No." Abu Hurayrah said: "I said: 'I refuse!'" Abu Salamah said: "By my life, Abu Hurayrah certainly used to narrate to us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is no contagious transmission.' So I do not know whether Abu Hurayrah forgot, or whether one of the two statements abrogated the other."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no evil omen in the night-bird, no influence of stars on rain, and no Safar."

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us, from Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri: Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Du'ali informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission." Then a Bedouin stood up... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yunus and Salih. And from Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, who said: al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, the nephew of Namir, narrated to me that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no Safar, and no night-bird."

Muhammad ibn Hatim and Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to me—they said: Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and others informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no bad omen, no Safar, and no evil omen in the night-bird." Then a Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah..." the like of the hadith of Yunus.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—and the wording is that of Abu al-Tahir—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; Ibn Shihab said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no contagious transmission, no Safar, and no evil omen in the night-bird." A Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about camels that are in the sand as if they were gazelles, then a mangy camel comes and mingles among them, making them all mangy?" He said: "Then who infected the first one?"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah: that Umar went out toward ash-Sham, and when he reached Sargh, news reached him that the epidemic had broken out in ash-Sham. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you hear of it in a land, do not enter it; and when it strikes a land while you are in it, do not depart fleeing from it." So Umar ibn al-Khattab turned back from Sargh. And from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdillah: that Umar only turned back with the people because of the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of transmission, except that he said: that Abdullah ibn al-Harith narrated to him, and did not say "Abdullah ibn Abdillah."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Ibn Rafi' said: narrated to us, and the other two said: informed us: Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, with this chain of transmission, similar to the hadith of Malik. And in the hadith of Ma'mar it was added: He said: And he also said to him: "Do you see that if he grazed the barren valley and left the fertile one, would you consider him incapable?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then journey on." He said: So he traveled until he reached Medina, and said: "This is the station," or he said: "This is the dwelling place, if Allah wills."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Abdillah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from Abdullah ibn Abbas: that Umar ibn al-Khattab set out for ash-Sham until, when he reached Sargh, the commanders of the armies met him—Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and his companions—and informed him that an epidemic had broken out in ash-Sham. Ibn Abbas said: Umar said: "Call for me the early Emigrants." So I called them, and he consulted them, informing them that an epidemic had broken out in ash-Sham. They differed: some of them said: "You have set out for a purpose, and we do not think you should turn back from it." And some of them said: "With you are the rest of the people and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and we do not think you should lead them toward this epidemic." So he said: "Leave me." Then he said: "Call for me the Ansar." So I called them for him, and he consulted them; they followed the path of the Emigrants and differed as they had differed. So he said: "Leave me." Then he said: "Call for me whoever is present here from the elders of Quraysh who emigrated at the time of the Conquest." So I called them, and not even two men differed; they said: "We think you should turn back with the people and not lead them into this epidemic." Thereupon Umar called out among the people: "I shall mount my riding beast in the morning, so do likewise." Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah said: "Fleeing from the decree of Allah?" Umar said: "If only someone other than you had said that, O Abu Ubaydah!"—for Umar disliked disagreeing with him—"Yes, we flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah. Consider: if you had camels and you descended into a valley with two slopes, one fertile and the other barren, is it not so that if you grazed them on the fertile slope, you would graze them by the decree of Allah, and if you grazed them on the barren slope, you would graze them by the decree of Allah?" He said: Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf arrived—he had been away attending to some personal need—and said: "I have knowledge concerning this. I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'If you hear of it in a land, do not enter it; and if it breaks out in a land where you are present, do not depart fleeing from it.'" He said: Thereupon Umar ibn al-Khattab praised Allah and then turned back.

Wahb ibn Baqiyyah narrated it to me: Khalid—meaning al-Tahhan—informed us, from al-Shaybani, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Malik, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to their hadith.
